passages.heading: MD&A
passages.text: FINANCIAL CONDITION AND RESULTS OF OPERATIONS This Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations generally discusses our 2025 and 2024 results and year-to-year comparisons between 2025 and 2024. Discussions of our 2024 results and year-to-year comparisons between 2024 and 2023 that are not included in this Annual Report on Form 10-K can be found in “Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations” in Part II, Item 7 of our Annual Report on Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2024, which was filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission on February 25, 2025. Overview We are one of the largest North American less-than-truckload (“LTL”) motor carriers. We provide regional, inter-regional and national LTL services through a single integrated, union-free organization. Our service offerings, which include expedited transportation, are provided through an expansive network of service centers located throughout the continental United States. Through strategic alliances, we also provide LTL services throughout North America. In addition to our core LTL services, we offer a range of value-added services including container drayage, truckload brokerage and supply chain consulting. More than 98% of our revenue has historically been derived from transporting LTL shipments for our customers, whose demand for our services is generally tied to industrial production and the overall health of the U.S. domestic economy. In analyzing the components of our revenue, we monitor changes and trends in our LTL volumes and LTL revenue per hundredweight. While LTL revenue per hundredweight is a yield measurement, it is also a commonly-used indicator for general pricing trends in the LTL industry. This yield metric is not a true measure of price, however, as it can be influenced by many other factors, such as changes in fuel surcharges, weight per shipment and length of haul. As a result, changes in revenue per hundredweight do not necessarily indicate actual changes in underlying base rates. LTL revenue per hundredweight and the key factors that can impact this metric are described in more detail below: • LTL Revenue Per Hundredweight - Our LTL transportation services are generally priced based on weight, commodity, and distance. This measurement reflects the application of our pricing policies to the services we provide, which are influenced by competitive market conditions and our growth objectives. Generally, freight is rated by a class system, which is established by the National Motor Freight Traffic Association, Inc. Light, bulky freight typically has a higher class and is priced at higher revenue per hundredweight than dense, heavy freight. Fuel surcharges, accessorial charges, revenue adjustments and revenue for undelivered freight are included in this measurement, and we regularly monitor the components that impact our pricing. The fuel surcharge is generally designed to offset fluctuations in the cost of our petroleum-based products and is indexed to diesel fuel prices published by the U.S. Department of Energy, which reset each week. passages.heading: Risk factors
passages.text: An investment in our common stock involves a variety of risks and uncertainties. The following describes some of the material risks that could adversely affect our business, financial condition, operating results or cash flows. We may also be adversely impacted by other risks not presently known to us or that we currently consider immaterial. Although the risks below are organized by headings and each risk is discussed separately, many are interrelated. Risks Related to our Business and Operations If we are unable to successfully execute our growth strategy, and develop, market and consistently deliver high-quality services that meet customer expectations, our business and future results of operations may suffer. Our growth strategy includes increasing the volume of freight moving through our existing service center network primarily by increasing our market share and selectively expanding our capacity in the United States. In connection with our growth strategy, at various times, we have consistently expanded and upgraded our service center network, purchased additional equipment and increased 6 our sales and marketing efforts, and we expect to continue to do so. Our growth strategy exposes us to a number of risks, including the following: • shortages of suitable real estate may limit our growth and could cause congestion in our service center network, which could result in increased operating expenses; • our projected freight volume growth may differ from actual results, and prior capital investments based on our projections may contribute to excess capacity that could negatively impact our profitability; • growth may strain our management, capital resources, information systems and customer service; • hiring new employees may increase training costs and may result in temporary inefficiencies until those employees become proficient in their jobs; • competition for qualified employees could adversely affect our profitability; • we may find it more difficult to maintain our unique OD Family culture, which we believe has been a key contributor to our success; • expanding our service offerings may require us to enter into new markets and encounter new competitive challenges; and • limited supply and increased costs of new equipment may adversely affect our profitability and cash flows. We cannot ensure that we will overcome the risks associated with our growth strategy. If we fail to overcome those risks, we may not realize projected growth and related revenue or profits from our efforts, we may incur additional expenses and, as a result, our financial position and results of operations could be materially and adversely affected. Various economic factors such as inflationary pressures or downturns in the domestic economy could adversely impact our profitability and cash flows. Inflationary pressures have been significant in the United States in recent years. Inflation impacts the cost to operate our business by putting upward pressure on wages, benefits, real estate, equipment, fuel, parts and repairs, insurance, and other general and miscellaneous expenses. credit_strengths.text: Old Dominion's net cash position, with cash exceeding reported debt, places leverage far below the Industrials sector median and supports a minimal indicative financial risk profile. This balance-sheet strength is reinforced by consistent operating profitability and substantial annual free cash flow generation, providing a deep cushion against cyclical freight demand swings.

Operating cash flow comfortably covers capital expenditure, leaving significant free cash flow after reinvestment. Interest coverage is exceptionally high, reflecting negligible interest expense relative to operating income. This cash-generation capacity underpins the company's ability to fund growth, dividends and buybacks without relying on external debt.

key_risks.text: The company's growth strategy relies on expanding its service center network and purchasing equipment, which exposes it to risks such as real estate shortages, freight volume shortfalls, and excess capacity that could pressure profitability. These risks are detailed in the risk factors and could materially affect financial condition if growth targets are not met.

Debt structure includes senior notes with scheduled principal amortization and a revolving credit agreement maturing in the medium term. While current debt is modest, upcoming maturities and potential refinancing needs warrant monitoring, especially if operating cash flow declines. The credit agreement's borrowing capacity provides flexibility but remains subject to lender discretion.

debt_servicing_capacity.text: Debt servicing is comfortably supported by operating cash flow, with free cash flow to debt exceeding sector norms. Interest coverage is exceptionally high, and the company maintains a net cash position, indicating ample capacity to meet obligations. The minimal leverage profile suggests debt service is not a near-term concern.

Liquidity is solid, with a current ratio above the sector median and a substantial cash balance. The company's revolving credit facility provides additional backup liquidity, though it remains uncommitted. Overall, debt servicing capacity is robust, with no material refinancing risk evident from the maturity profile.

overall_credit_view.text: Old Dominion exhibits a very strong credit profile, characterized by minimal leverage, net cash, and robust cash flow generation. The indicative financial risk profile is minimal, and key credit metrics compare favorably to sector medians. The company's consistent profitability and conservative balance sheet support a stable credit outlook.

While the company faces cyclical demand and growth execution risks, its financial flexibility and cash generation provide a strong buffer. Shareholder distributions absorb a portion of free cash flow, but remaining cash flow supports reinvestment and debt service. We view the credit as well-positioned to withstand industry downturns.

credit_strengths.text: Old Dominion 的淨現金狀況，即現金超過報告債務，使其槓桿遠低於工業行業中位數，並支持極低的指示性財務風險狀況。此資產負債表實力得到持續經營盈利能力和大量年度自由現金流產生的強化，為週期性貨運需求波動提供了深厚緩衝。
經營現金流輕鬆覆蓋資本支出，在再投資後留下大量自由現金流。利息覆蓋率極高，反映利息支出相對於經營收入微不足道。此現金產生能力支撐公司無需依賴外部債務即可為增長、股息和回購提供資金的能力。

key_risks.text: 公司的增長策略依賴於擴展其服務中心網絡和購買設備，這使其面臨房地產短缺、貨運量不足和產能過剩等風險，可能對盈利能力造成壓力。這些風險在風險因素中詳細說明，若增長目標未達成，可能對財務狀況產生重大影響。
債務結構包括有預定本金攤還的高級票據和中期到期的循環信貸協議。雖然當前債務適度，但即將到期的債務和潛在再融資需求值得監控，尤其是在經營現金流下降的情況下。信貸協議的借款能力提供靈活性，但仍受貸款人酌情決定權限制。

debt_servicing_capacity.text: 債務償還得到經營現金流的輕鬆支持，自由現金流對債務比率超過行業標準。利息覆蓋率極高，公司維持淨現金狀況，表明有充足能力履行義務。極低的槓桿狀況表明債務償還並非近期關注點。
流動性穩健，流動比率高於行業中位數，且現金餘額可觀。公司的循環信貸設施提供額外備用流動性，儘管其仍未承諾。總體而言，債務償還能力強勁，從到期情況看無明顯再融資風險。

overall_credit_view.text: Old Dominion 展現非常強勁的信用狀況，其特點是極低槓桿、淨現金和強勁的現金流產生。指示性財務風險狀況極低，關鍵信用指標與行業中位數相比有利。公司持續的盈利能力和保守的資產負債表支持穩定的信用展望。
雖然公司面臨週期性需求和增長執行風險，但其財務靈活性和現金產生提供了強大緩衝。股東分配吸收了部分自由現金流，但剩餘現金流支持再投資和債務償還。我們認為該信用狀況良好，能夠抵禦行業低迷。
